simple.meaning: מָעַךְ (mâʻak) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to press , i.e. to pierce , emasculate , handle.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Leviticus, 1 Samuel, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 22:24. The surrounding contexts include land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָעַךְ (H4600) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָעַךְ (mâʻak) / H4600 is traced through Leviticus 22:24, 1 Samuel 26:7, Ezekiel 23:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4600. maak [ מָעַךְ ] verb press, squeeze (Late Hebrew id. ; מְעַךְ ᵑ7 ; Arabic rub ); — Qal Passive participle וְכָרוּת וְנָתוּק וְכָתוּת וּמָעוּךְ Lev 22:24 (H), not to be offered to ׳י , reference to emasculation (compare Di); מְעוּכָהבָֿאָרֶץ וַחֲנִיתוֺ 1Sam 26:7 and his spear pressed (thrust) into the ground. Pu`al Perfect 3masculine plural שְׁדֵיהֶן מֹעֲכוּ שָׁמָּה Ezek 23:3 there were their breasts squeezed (|| עִשּׂוּ ; unchastely; figurative of intercourse of Samaria and Jerusalem with Egypt, involving idolatry).
